classifications.rationale: The President directs executive agencies to govern UAS information practices consistently with existing law; the segment describes internal administration and existing legal obligations rather than itself changing rights or status.
classifications.evidence: information must be collected, used, retained, and disseminated consistent with the Constitution, Federal law, and other applicable regulations and policies

classifications.rationale: Agencies must periodically review and, when necessary, update internal UAS policies; no specified legal consequence is imposed immediately or required later.
classifications.evidence: agencies shall, prior to deployment of new UAS technology and at least every 3 years, examine their existing UAS policies and procedures

classifications.rationale: The segment inseparably combines present operational duties governing collection, retention, and dissemination with internal oversight and transparency measures and a mandate to impose a later grant-funding condition on governmental recipients.
classifications.evidence: require that State, local, tribal, and territorial government recipients of Federal grant funding for the purchase or use of UAS for their own operations have in place policies and procedures

classifications.rationale: Agencies are directed to report to the President and publish access information on their policies, both administrative reporting and transparency functions without a substantive legal consequence.
classifications.evidence: agencies shall provide the President with a status report on the implementation of this section

classifications.rationale: The segment establishes and assigns an executive-led stakeholder process, defines terms for internal implementation, and preserves existing laws and policies; these are organizational and administrative measures.
classifications.evidence: There is hereby established a multi-stakeholder engagement process to develop and communicate best practices
